meta.question: Parking: when might demand exceed available aircraft parking space?
meta.how_to_read: Daily ramp demand comes from the parking model: 10,000 simulated weeks per scenario on the FAA-based forecast. P50 is the median day, P10-P90 the likely range, prob_over_normal_capacity the share of simulated weeks in which demand exceeds the ramp that day.
meta.human_in_command: The model recommends; a named manager approves every action. It never accepts, refuses or reassigns an individual aircraft. Overflow is a flag for a person to resolve.

situation_outlook.base_case_note: The model's base case is the forecast demand with the game-day security pause applied, because every Super Bowl has had a security flight restriction. Daily parking totals equal normal operations; the pause changes when aircraft can move on game day.

items.basis: Every Super Bowl has a security flight restriction; under the 2022 (LVI) precedent LAX sat inside the inner ring, so private (Part 91) flights are grounded for the window. No 2027 notice is published yet.
5% of February days at LAX had heavy rain (NOAA GHCN-Daily LAX x FAA daily operations, 2016-2019 and 2023-2025, vs dry days of the same weekday and month). The model tests it on game day.
No measured likelihood. Tests what happens if departures slip a full day after the game.
Same demand without any situation, for comparison.

levers.human_in_command: Offers only. Every action needs approval by the named role. The system never accepts, rejects or cancels an individual aircraft.
levers.take_up_status: unknown; shown as a range, not a forecast

Low.not_recommended: At 30% take-up, a cheap Thu-Fri slot moves the game-day P50 from 13.5 to 13.3 su and unaccommodated aircraft from 1.0 to 2.1: aircraft arrive earlier but leave at the same time, so they stay longer. It does not free parking.
Low.note: Past Super Bowls filled parking without raising prices (alan/docs/lax_private_capacity_and_cost_research.md); reservations (PPR) stay the primary tool, incentives are offers, and the system never refuses an aircraft.

recommended.action: Offer a $500 drop-and-go credit to Super Bowl arrivals Thu-Sun: drop passengers, reposition to a partner field, return for pickup
recommended.rationale: Without action 2.3 aircraft a run do not fit the 15 su ramp. If 10% of event arrivals accept: 2.0, net $380; if 30% accept: 1.6, net $1,002. Complements the ramp plan (tow-in packing, overflow lease); take-up is unknown

Medium.not_recommended: At 30% take-up, a cheap Thu-Fri slot moves the game-day P50 from 17.4 to 17.3 su and unaccommodated aircraft from 2.3 to 4.3: aircraft arrive earlier but leave at the same time, so they stay longer. It does not free parking.
Medium.note: Past Super Bowls filled parking without raising prices (alan/docs/lax_private_capacity_and_cost_research.md); reservations (PPR) stay the primary tool, incentives are offers, and the system never refuses an aircraft.

recommended.action: Offer a $500 drop-and-go credit to Super Bowl arrivals Thu-Sun: drop passengers, reposition to a partner field, return for pickup
recommended.rationale: Without action 6.0 aircraft a run do not fit the 15 su ramp. If 10% of event arrivals accept: 5.4, net $1,116; if 30% accept: 4.2, net $3,112. Complements the ramp plan (tow-in packing, overflow lease); take-up is unknown

High.not_recommended: At 30% take-up, a cheap Thu-Fri slot moves the game-day P50 from 23.0 to 23.0 su and unaccommodated aircraft from 6.0 to 7.9: aircraft arrive earlier but leave at the same time, so they stay longer. It does not free parking.
High.note: Past Super Bowls filled parking without raising prices (alan/docs/lax_private_capacity_and_cost_research.md); reservations (PPR) stay the primary tool, incentives are offers, and the system never refuses an aircraft.

demand_levels.basis: ramp utilization at the daily P50 peak (risk_level in elia/resource_requirements.csv)

ramp_aircraft.note: Median number of aircraft of each size on the ramp at each day's peak, and median arrivals and departures per size, from the same 10,000 simulated weeks as the parking model (parking_kit/ramp_aircraft.py, which reproduces parking_demand_su_p50 exactly). Use these counts for the planes shown.

capacity.derivation: Atlantic's ramp: 52600 m2 x 0.85 usable / 600.0 m2 per su = 75 su, scaled to this FBO's 10% share vs Atlantic's 50%: 15 su. Estimated, not a measured stand count.

aircraft.space_unit: 1 su = one light-jet parking position (about 600 m2 including clearance and half a taxilane)

light.example: Citation CJ3 (16.3 m span x 15.6 m)

stays.class: assumed (illustrative stay mix from the team ledger)

hourly_profile.note: Hour-of-day shares are a placeholder curve, not observed data.

game_day_restriction.status: assumption from the Super Bowl LVI precedent; no 2027 notice published
